method_card.title: Tourist Attractions and Eating Out
method_card.content:
This lesson combines tourist-attraction vocabulary with restaurant language — two topics that frequently appear together in holiday writing tasks and speaking role plays.

GermanEnglish
die Sehenswürdigkeit (-en)tourist sight / place of interest
das Museum (-en)museum
das Schloss (-̈er)castle / palace
der Dom / die Kathedralecathedral
die Stadtführungguided city tour
die Speisekartemenu
die Rechnungbill
der Kellner / die Kellnerinwaiter / waitress
die Vorspeisestarter
das Hauptgerichtmain course
der Nachtischdessert
das Hähnchenchicken
die Bratwurstfried sausage
das Schnitzelbreaded cutlet
leckerdelicious

Grammar focus — accusative case for ordering: After ich nehme and ich hätte gern, the noun is in the accusative case. Masculine nouns change: der Fisch → den Fisch, der Salat → den Salat. Neuter and feminine stay the same in the accusative: das Hähnchen → das Hähnchen, die Suppe → die Suppe.

Grammar focus — past tense for tourist visits: Use the perfect tense to describe what you did: Wir haben ein Schloss besichtigt (haben — transitive). Note: besichtigen has inseparable prefix be- → past participle takes NO ge-: besichtigt.

Model paragraph: Wir haben eine Stadtführung gemacht und das alte Schloss besichtigt. Am Abend sind wir in ein Restaurant gegangen. Ich hätte gern das Schnitzel mit Kartoffeln, bitte. Es hat fantastisch geschmeckt! (We did a city tour and visited the old castle. In the evening we went to a restaurant. I would like the schnitzel with potatoes, please. It tasted fantastic!)
steps: Learn tourist-attraction nouns with their genders (die Sehenswürdigkeit, das Schloss, der Dom)
Master polite ordering phrases: Ich hätte gern + accusative and Ich nehme + accusative
Practise the perfect tense for describing visits: haben + besucht/besichtigt/gesehen
Build restaurant role-play responses using Sie register and accusative for food orders

exam_context.frequency: High-frequency topic — tourist activities and restaurant visits appear in writing tasks, picture cards and role plays

worked_examples.question: Translate into English: 'Könnte ich bitte die Speisekarte haben?'

steps.label: Identify the polite request
steps.content: Könnte ich = Could I — this is the Konjunktiv II (conditional) form, a polite way to ask.

steps.label: Key vocabulary
steps.content: die Speisekarte = the menu. bitte = please. haben = to have.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Could I have the menu, please?

worked_examples.question: Translate into German: 'I ate a delicious soup and drank an orange juice.' (Check gender and case.)

steps.label: First clause
steps.content: 'I ate' = Ich habe … gegessen (perfect tense, haben). 'A delicious soup' = eine leckere Suppe — die Suppe is feminine, accusative, indefinite article eine, adjective ending -e.

steps.label: Second clause
steps.content: 'I drank' = Ich habe … getrunken. 'An orange juice' = einen Orangensaft — der Orangensaft is masculine, accusative → einen.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Ich habe eine leckere Suppe gegessen und einen Orangensaft getrunken.

bronze.question: Match the German to the English meaning
Match the German to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct polite ordering form
sentence_parts: gern das Hähnchen mit Pommes, bitte.

gaps.rule: Polite ordering — ich hätte gern (Konjunktiv II of haben)
gaps.correct_explain: hätte gern = I would like. This is the Konjunktiv II form — used for polite ordering.

wrong.habe: habe is present indicative ('I have'). For polite ordering use hätte gern.
wrong.hat: hat is the er/sie/es form. For ich + polite ordering, use hätte.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct past participle

gaps.rule: Past participle of besuchen — inseparable prefix, no ge-
gaps.correct_explain: besucht is the past participle of besuchen (to visit). Inseparable prefix be- means NO ge- is added.

wrong.gebesucht: Wrong — besuchen starts with the inseparable prefix be-. No ge- is added: besucht.
wrong.besuchen: besuchen is the infinitive. You need the past participle: besucht.

gaps.rule: Past participle of besichtigen — inseparable prefix be-, no ge-
gaps.correct_explain: besichtigt is the past participle of besichtigen (to visit/view). Inseparable prefix be- → no ge-.

wrong.gebesichtigt: Wrong — besichtigen has the inseparable prefix be-. No ge-: besichtigt.

bronze.question: What does 'Ich möchte mich beschweren' mean?
options: I would like to make a complaint
I would like to order dessert
I would like the bill please
I would like a table for two

bronze.question: What does 'Das Essen war ausgezeichnet' mean?

model_answers: I ordered a schnitzel with potato salad. It was very delicious!

silver.question: Complete the sentence (no word bank)
silver.english: I **ordered** chicken and I **drank** a mineral water.

gaps.rule: Past participle of bestellen — inseparable prefix be-, no ge-
gaps.correct_explain: bestellt is the past participle of bestellen. Verbs with inseparable prefixes (be-, ver-, er-, etc.) do NOT add ge-.

wrong.gebestellt: Wrong — bestellen has the inseparable prefix be-. No ge-: bestellt.

gaps.correct_explain: getrunken is the irregular past participle of trinken (to drink).

wrong.getrinkt: There is no form getrinkt. Trinken is irregular: getrunken.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Ich möchte ein Tasse Kaffee bestellen.
silver.explanation: Tasse is feminine (die Tasse), so the accusative indefinite article is eine, not ein (which is used for neuter/masculine).
silver.translation: I would like to order a cup of coffee.

silver.question: Build the sentence in German
silver.english: Could I have the menu, please?

distractor_labels.kann: wrong mood — kann is present indicative; Könnte is Konjunktiv II (polite conditional). Use Könnte for requests.

silver.source_text: I would like to order the fish with rice, please.
model_answers: Ich möchte den Fisch mit Reis bestellen, bitte.
Ich hätte gern den Fisch mit Reis, bitte.

gold.source_text: Last week I went to a restaurant with my family. I ordered a schnitzel with potato salad and it tasted delicious. I would like to go back next year.
model_answers: Letzte Woche bin ich mit meiner Familie in ein Restaurant gegangen. Ich habe ein Schnitzel mit Kartoffelsalat bestellt und es hat lecker geschmeckt. Ich möchte nächstes Jahr wieder hingehen.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a translation from English to German. Source: '{source}'. Model answer: '{model}'. Check: sein for gehen (movement verb: bin gegangen); haben for bestellen (transitive: habe bestellt — no ge- on bestellt because of inseparable be-); es hat geschmeckt (dative subject 'it' for taste); möchte + infinitive at end (hingehen is separable — correct as one word in infinitive). Accept valid alternatives. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"2-3 sentences","improvement":"optional specific correction"}

gold.question: Build the sentence in German
gold.english: I am allergic to nuts — do you have anything without nuts?

distractor_labels.du: wrong register — in a restaurant you use the formal Sie, not informal du.
distractor_labels.mit: wrong preposition — ohne means 'without'; mit means 'with'. We need 'without nuts'.
distractor_labels.bist: wrong form — bist is the du form; Ich takes bin.

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a restaurant in Germany with your family. The waiter comes to take your order.

bullets.prompt: Greet the waiter and ask for a table for three people.
bullets.model_answer: Guten Abend! Haben Sie einen Tisch für drei Personen, bitte?
bullets.note: formal greeting + Haben Sie (Sie register) + accusative einen Tisch (masculine: der Tisch → den/einen)

bullets.prompt: Order a main course and a drink using a polite form.
bullets.model_answer: Ich hätte gern das Hähnchen mit Reis und eine Cola, bitte.
bullets.note: Ich hätte gern (polite Konjunktiv II) + accusative das Hähnchen (neuter — stays das); eine Cola (feminine — stays eine)

bullets.prompt: Complain that the food is cold and ask for something different.
bullets.model_answer: Entschuldigung, das Essen ist kalt. Könnte ich bitte ein anderes Gericht bekommen?
bullets.note: nicht is not used here — adjective 'kalt' after ist; Könnte ich (polite Konjunktiv II request); ein anderes Gericht (neuter accusative — strong adjective ending -es)

bullets.prompt: Ask for the bill and say the service was excellent.
bullets.model_answer: Die Rechnung, bitte. Der Service war ausgezeichnet, vielen Dank!
bullets.note: Die Rechnung (definite article — feminine); war ausgezeichnet (predicative adjective, no ending)

gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking a restaurant role play. The student must use Sie register throughout — a restaurant is a formal transactional context. For each bullet, assess: (1) Did they communicate the required information? (2) Is the German grammatically accurate? Check: Sie register (Haben Sie, Könnte ich), polite forms (hätte gern, möchte), accusative articles for food (den Fisch, das Hähnchen, die Suppe), kalt as predicative adjective (no ending). Award marks out of 10. Be encouraging. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"Per-bullet feedback","improvement":"Key grammar point to revise"}

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in German about a restaurant visit on holiday. Include: where you went and with whom, what you ordered (using a polite form), your opinion of the food, and what you would do differently next time.
gold.ai_system_prompt: You are a GCSE German examiner marking extended writing about a restaurant visit. Mark on: Communication (all four points addressed?), Range of language (past tense for visit — bin gegangen (sein) and habe bestellt (haben), polite ordering with hätte gern/möchte, opinion structures, conditional for next time with würde or möchte), Accuracy (accusative articles for food items, perfect tense auxiliary choice — sein for gehen, haben for bestellen/essen, past participles at clause end, noun capitalisation). Be encouraging and formative. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}

model_answers: Wenn ich könnte, würde ich jeden Tag in einem Restaurant essen, weil das Essen immer lecker ist.
